raw_text:
Great. Below is a structured 12-week program designed for a 45-year-old female with type 2 diabetes (on metformin, HbA1c 7.2). It emphasizes fat loss and glycemic control, includes a full-gym resistance and cardio plan, and provides nutrition guidance with diabetic considerations. Adjustments should be made in real time based on glucose responses, injuries, and fitness progress. Always coordinate with her healthcare provider before starting, especially around medication, blood glucose targets, and any hypoglycemia risk.

Overview
- Goals: fat loss, improved insulin sensitivity, better glycemic control, sustainable exercise habit.
- Weekly structure: 4 resistance sessions + 2 cardio sessions + 1 optional mobility/activated recovery day. One deload week every 4th week.
- Intensity ranges: Resistance sets at 60–75% 1RM for most work; occasional 8–12 RM finisher. Cardio in moderate intensity (roughly 60–75% of max heart rate) with some low-intensity steady state (LISS) and one optional interval session if glucose control allows.
- Progression: progressive overload across 12 weeks via increased reps, load, or volume, while maintaining form and safety.
- Nutrition approach: moderate caloric deficit, macronutrient targets supportive of glycemic control, fiber emphasis, carbohydrate timing around workouts, and diabetes-specific considerations (carb consistency, monitoring, metformin implications, hypoglycemia safety).

Phase structure by week
- Phase 1: Weeks 1–3 (Adaptation and stability)
- Phase 2: Weeks 4–6 (Progressive overload and nutrition tightening)
- Phase 3: Weeks 7–9 (Fat loss emphasis and higher training stimulus)
- Phase 4: Weeks 10–12 (Peak fat loss, conditioning, and taper into maintenance)

Details by week (sessions per week)
- Session A: Upper body resistance
- Session B: Lower body resistance
- Session C: Push–pull total body
- Session D: Cardio focused + mobility
- Session E: Optional cardio/active recovery
- Sessions 6 days per week total, with one rest day (adjust as needed)

Resistance training template (adjust order as available)
- Tempo: 2–0–2 on primary lifts; 2–0–3 on eccentric-focused work if desired. Reps are counts to concentric plus controlled eccentric.
- Rest: 60–90 seconds between sets for hypertrophy work; up to 2 minutes for complex lifts or heavy compounds.
- Warm-up: 5–10 minutes of light cardio and dynamic mobility; activation work for glutes, rotator cuff, and core stability.

Week-by-week plan (detailed)

Weeks 1–3: Adaptation and stability
Goal: Establish technique, baseline strength, insulin-friendly energy balance, and habit formation.

Session A – Upper body
- Bench press or chest press: 3x10–12
- Lat pulldown or assisted pull-up: 3x10–12
- Seated row: 3x10–12
- Dumbbell shoulder press: 3x12
- Dumbbell curls: 2x12
- Triceps pushdown: 2x12
- Core: planks 3x30–40 seconds

Session B – Lower body
- Goblet squat or leg press: 3x12
- Romanian deadlift or stiff-leg deadlift: 3x10–12
- Leg extension: 3x12
- Hamstring curl: 3x12
- Calf raise: 3x15
- Core: dead bug 3x12 per side

Session C – Push–pull total body
- Barbell or dumbbell bench press: 3x10–12
- Barbell row or dumbbell row: 3x10–12
- Overhead press: 3x10–12
- Dumbbell lateral raises: 3x12
- Farmers walk or suitcase carry: 2 rounds x 30–40 seconds
- Core: bicycle crunches 3x15 per side

Cardio Day (Session D)
- 25–35 minutes moderate-intensity cardio (cycle, treadmill, elliptical) at a pace where conversation is possible but challenging.
- Optional: 6–8 x 1-minute brisk intervals with 1-minute easy recovery if glucose allows and supervised.

Mobility/Recovery (Session E optional)
- 20–30 minutes of mobility work focusing on hips, ankles, thoracic spine; light yoga flow; breathwork.

Weeks 4–6: Progressive overload and nutrition tightening
Adjust loads upward by 5–10% where technique remains solid; increase volume modestly if tolerating.

Session A – Upper body
- Bench press or chest press: 4x8–10
- Lat pulldown: 4x8–10
- Seated row: 3x10–12
- Dumbbell shoulder press: 3x10–12
- Incline dumbbell press: 3x10
- Triceps pushdown: 3x12
- Core: pallof press 3x12 per side

Session B – Lower body
- Back squat or leg press: 4x8–10
- Romanian deadlift: 3x8–10
- Leg curl: 3x12
- Leg extension: 3x12
- Calf raise: 3x15
- Core: hanging leg raise or knee tucks 3x12

Session C – Push–pull total body
- Barbell or dumbbell bench: 4x8–10
- Barbell row: 4x8–10
- Push-ups or landmine press: 3x10–12
- Lat pulldown: 3x10–12
- Face pulls: 3x12
- Farmer’s carry: 2x40 seconds

Cardio Day
- 30–40 minutes moderate intensity or 20–25 minutes interval work (e.g., 2–4 x 2 minutes hard with 2 minutes easy), depending on glucose response.

Nutrition guidance weeks 1–6
- Calorie target: modest deficit of 250–500 kcal/day from maintenance; adjust based on weekly weight trend and appetite.
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg body weight per day to support satiety and glycemic control.
- Fat: 25–35% of total calories; emphasize unsaturated fats; limit trans fats.
- Carbs: distribute evenly across day with emphasis around workouts; aim for 2–3 fiber-rich, minimally processed carb sources per meal.
- Fiber: at least 25–30 g/day.
- Hydration: 30–35 ml/kg/day; adjust for activity and climate.
- Glycemic targets: aim for stable fasting glucose in the 90–130 mg/dL range; aim postprandial peaks to stay below 180 mg/dL when possible.
- Carbohydrate timing:
  - Pre-workout: 20–40 g fast-diber carb 30–60 minutes before if training in the morning or if glucose is low to moderate.
  - Post-workout: 1–1.5 g/kg body weight of carbs within 1–2 hours after training to replenish glycogen and support recovery; combine with protein.
  - Evenly distribute carbohydrates across meals to prevent large post-meal glucose spikes; prefer low-glycemic or steady- release carbs (oats, quinoa, beans, lentils, vegetables, whole fruits).
- Monitoring: recommend keeping a log of meals and glucose (if possible), noting blood glucose before meals and 1–2 hours after meals and workouts. Hypoglycemia risk around metformin is lower than with sulfonylureas or insulin, but watch for symptoms—carry fast-acting carbs.

Weeks 7–9: Fat loss emphasis and higher stimulus
Adjust to maintain progression while increasing metabolic demand and refining nutrition.

Session A – Upper body
- Incline bench press: 4x6–8
- Pull-ups or assisted pull-ups: 4x6–8
- Seated row: 4x8–10
- Standing overhead press: 3x8–10
- Lateral raises: 3x12–15
- Triceps extension: 3x12
- Core: ab wheel rollout or dead bug 3x12

Session B – Lower body
- Front squat or goblet with tempo: 4x6–8
- Romanian deadlift: 3x8–10
- Bulgarian split squat: 3x8–10 per leg
- Leg curl: 3x12
- Calf raise: 4x15–20
- Core: side planks 3x30–40 seconds each side

Session C – Push–pull total body
- Dumbbell or barbell bench: 4x6–8
- Barbell row or single-arm row: 4x6–8
- Push press: 3x6–8
- Face pulls: 3x12–15
- Farmer’s carry: 3 rounds x 40–60 seconds

Cardio Day
- 35–45 minutes at moderate intensity or 20 minutes of intervals (2–3 minutes hard, 2 minutes easy) with an emphasis on consistency.

Weeks 10–12: Peak fat loss and conditioning
Primary aim is consistent training quality with a slight reduction in overall volume for recovery, maintaining muscle mass.

Session A – Upper body
- Flat bench press: 4x5–7
- Lat pulldown: 4x6–8
- Seated row: 3x8–10
- Overhead press: 3x6–8
- Chest fly (machine or dumbbell): 3x10–12
- Triceps pushdown: 3x12
- Core: cable anti-rotation or Pallof 3x12 per side

Session B – Lower body
- Back squat: 4x5–7
- Deadlift variation (conventional or sumo): 3x5–7
- Leg press or hack squat: 3x8–10
- Hamstring curl: 3x12
- Calf raise: 4x12–15
- Core: ab wheel or reverse crunch 3x12

Session C – Push–pull total body
- Barbell bench or push-up tempo: 4x6–8
- Barbell or dumbbell row: 4x6–8
- Push press: 3x6–8
- Lateral raises: 3x12
- Farmer’s carry: 3 rounds x 40–60 seconds

Cardio Day
- 30–40 minutes, mix of steady-state and optional intervals if glucose control is stable.

Recovery and deload
- Week 4 and Week 8: deload week with reduced volume (60–70%) and light cardio only; focus on technique, mobility, and sleep.
- Ensure at least one full rest day per week; consider active recovery on lower-intensity days if fatigue is high.

Injury prevention and safety
- Prioritize technique; use a trainer during new movements for the first sessions.
- Stop if sharp pain or dizziness occurs; monitor glucose around workouts.
- Include a brief cool-down with light stretching and breath work after every session.
- Sleep aim: 7–9 hours per night; manage stress through mindfulness or breathing routines.

Glycemic monitoring and metformin considerations
- If hypoglycemia risk is present, carry a fast-acting carbohydrate (e.g., glucose tablets) and have a plan with the client for how to respond.
- If fasting glucose exceeds target consistently (e.g., >180 mg/dL), consider adjusting carbohydrate distribution or consult with the client’s healthcare provider.
- Metformin effects: generally does not cause hypoglycemia by itself; exercise increases insulin sensitivity, which can improve glycemic control. Monitor for GI upset with metformin and meals—move to extended-release formulation if needed and tolerated.

Sample daily structure (example for a training day)
- Pre-workout nutrition: 20–30 g protein, 20–40 g carbs; low fat if GI intolerance.
- Post-workout: 20–40 g protein, 40–60 g carbs (adjust to body weight and intensity).
- Meals: 3 main meals with 1–2 snacks, centering around vegetables, lean proteins, whole grains or legumes, healthy fats.
- Hydration: water always; consider electrolytes if sessions are long or very hot.

Example weekly schedule
- Monday: Session A (Upper)
- Tuesday: Session B (Lower)
- Wednesday: Session C (Push–pull)
- Thursday: Cardio Day + Mobility
- Friday: Session A or D variant (depending on rotation) or optional light cardio
- Saturday: Session B or C variant
- Sunday: Rest or active recovery

KPIs and progression tracking
- Week 1 baseline: record 1RM estimates (or performance estimates) for key lifts: bench, squat, deadlift, row.
- Weekly: track sets/reps and loads; aim for small increases (2.5–5% thresholds) every 1–2 weeks, or add 1–2 reps if load cannot safely increase.
- Body composition: weigh weekly, same time, same clothes; measure waist circumference every 4 weeks.
- Glycemic metrics: track fasting glucose and post-meal glucose 1–2 hours after meals for patterns. Adjust nutrition based on trends.

Final notes
- This plan is a framework. Please customize to her available equipment, preferences, and any medical advice from her clinician.
- Maintain open communication about energy levels, appetite, body shape changes, and glucose responses. If any issues arise (poor sleep, illness, injuries), adjust volume and intensity accordingly.
- If she wants, I can translate this into a weekly printable plan with exact exercise order, rest intervals, and daily nutrition templates tailored to her current body weight and macronutrient targets.
